posts.why: The features/outcomes distinction is the day's spine.

tiktok.hook: Eighteen features, and not one sentence about what you can do.
beats: But what do I do on Monday
tiktok.vo: This sales page lists eighteen features: templates, modules, formats, a private community, lifetime access. Not once does it say what you will be able to do on Monday morning that you cannot do today. Features describe the object. Outcomes describe the person. Customers buy the second one and use the first one to justify it.
tiktok.cap: Eighteen features. Zero sentences about what you can do afterwards.
tiktok.body: Eighteen features and not one sentence about what the buyer can do on Monday that they cannot do today. Features describe the object; outcomes describe the person, and people buy the second.

instagram.cap:
The fix is not to remove the features, it is to put one sentence above them: after this, you will be able to ____. Everything below becomes supporting evidence.

Features justify. Outcomes sell.

facebook.body:
A sales page I read lists eighteen features: templates, modules, formats, a community, lifetime access.

Not once does it say what you will be able to do on Monday that you cannot do today.

Features describe the object. Outcomes describe the person. Customers buy the second and use the first to justify it.

What is your outcome sentence?

posts.topic: A bundle that is one PDF
posts.why: Sets an honesty bar the audience can hold sellers to.

tiktok.hook: A bundle that is one PDF is a lie with good design.
tiktok.vo: A bundle that turns out to be one PDF is a lie with good design, and it happens constantly. So before you buy anything called a bundle, ask for the file list: names, formats, count. Ours is thirty six files across nine packs, and I am happy to be counted, because the count is the only claim you can check before you pay.
tiktok.cap: Ask for the file list before you pay. Names, formats, count. Ours is 36.
tiktok.body: Before buying anything called a bundle, ask for the file list: names, formats, count. Ours is thirty-six files across nine packs, and the count is the only claim you can check before paying.

instagram.cap:
Any seller who will not list the files is telling you something. It is usually that the list is short.

A count you can verify before paying is worth more than any testimonial.

facebook.body:
A 'bundle' that turns out to be one PDF is a lie with good design, and it happens constantly.

So before you buy anything called a bundle, ask for the file list: names, formats, count.

Ours is 36 files across nine packs. Count them.

The count is the only claim you can check before you pay.

What is the last bundle you bought?

posts.why: Turns transparency into a repeatable sales page structure.

tiktok.hook: Show the file list, not the promise. Names, formats, count.
tiktok.vo: Show the file list instead of the promise. Names, formats, count, in a plain list, on the page, before anybody pays. It is not beautiful and it is not aspirational, and it is the part of a sales page that closes, because a list is evidence and a promise is atmosphere. Every mystery box is asking you to trust the box.
tiktok.cap: A plain file list closes more than a paragraph of promises.
tiktok.body: Names, formats, count, in a plain list, before anybody pays. Not beautiful, not aspirational, and it is the part of the page that closes — a list is evidence, a promise is atmosphere.

instagram.cap:
You can apply this to your own offer immediately: write the inventory, not the adjectives. Six bullets will do more than a hero image.

Mystery boxes ask for trust they have not earned.

facebook.body:
Show the file list, not the promise.

Names. Formats. Count. In a plain list, on the page, before anybody pays.

It is not beautiful and it is not aspirational, and it is the part of a sales page that actually closes — because a list is evidence and a promise is atmosphere.

What is your inventory?

posts.why: Removes the need for persuasive tricks.

tiktok.hook: Transparency is the whole sales page. Nobody trusts a mystery box.
tiktok.vo: Transparency about what is inside is the entire sales page. What is inside, what it costs, what it will not do. Those three things, in that order, and you have a page. Everything else is decoration people add because they are nervous about the price, and the nervousness is more visible than the price.
tiktok.cap: Inside, price, limits. That is a sales page. The rest is nerves.
tiktok.body: What is inside, what it costs, what it will not do. Three things, in that order, and you have a page. The rest is decoration people add because they are nervous about the price.

instagram.cap:
If you find yourself writing a fourth paragraph about the transformation, that is usually a sign you are unsure the inventory is strong enough.

Nervousness about a price is more visible than the price.

facebook.body:
Transparency about what is inside is the entire sales page.

What is inside. What it costs. What it will not do.

Those three, in that order, and you have a page. Everything else is decoration people add because they are nervous about the price — and the nervousness is more visible than the price.

What is missing from yours?

posts.topic: She asked to see page one
posts.why: A small risk that paid off, told plainly.

tiktok.hook: A buyer asked to see page one before paying. She bought.
tiktok.vo: Someone asked to see page one of the homepage pack before paying five thousand naira. We sent a screenshot of the actual page, no watermark, no tease. She bought about four minutes later and said she had been burned before by something that looked good on the cover. Sending one page cost us nothing and did what no testimonial could, because it was the thing itself.
tiktok.cap: She asked for page one. We sent it. She bought four minutes later.
tiktok.body: One screenshot of the actual page, no watermark, no tease. She bought four minutes later saying she had been burned by covers before. The thing itself beats any description of it.

instagram.cap:
If you are not willing to show one page before payment, ask yourself whether that is because it is precious or because it is thin.

Show the actual thing. It is the cheapest proof you own.

facebook.body:
Someone asked to see page one of the homepage pack before paying ₦5,000.

We sent a screenshot of the actual page. No watermark. No tease.

She bought about four minutes later and said she had been burned before by something that looked good on the cover.

Showing one page cost us nothing and did what no testimonial could, because it was the thing itself.

What could you show?

posts.why: A single asset that removes most buyer doubt.

tiktok.hook: Publish your contents page. It closes more than a testimonial.
tiktok.vo: Publish the contents page of whatever you sell, publicly, with no email required. Every chapter title, every file name, in order. It closes more than a testimonial because it is the only proof a stranger can evaluate without trusting you, and it costs you one screenshot. The people who steal from a contents page were never going to buy the contents.
tiktok.cap: One screenshot of the contents page. More persuasive than praise.
tiktok.body: Every chapter title, every file name, in order, public, no email required. It is the only proof a stranger can evaluate without trusting you, and it costs one screenshot.

instagram.cap:
An outline shows how much thinking went into the thing. A cover shows how much budget went into the design.

People who steal an outline were never buying the outline.

facebook.body:
Publish the contents page of whatever you sell. Publicly. No email required.

Every chapter title, every file name, in order.

It closes more than a testimonial, because it is the only proof a stranger can evaluate without trusting you first.

And it costs one screenshot.

What is on your contents page?

posts.why: Undercuts the bundle's own selling point, which is disarming.

tiktok.hook: Thirty-six files is not better than six. Only if you use them.
tiktok.vo: Thirty six files is not automatically better than six. It is a fact about the product, not a benefit to you, and I say that about my own bundle. The benefit is that one of them is the file you actually needed, and if six would have done it, buy six. Volume is easy to produce and hard to use, which is why it makes such a good-looking number.
tiktok.cap: More files is a fact. Using one is the benefit. Buy the smaller thing if it fits.
tiktok.body: Volume is easy to produce and hard to use, which is exactly why it makes such a good-looking number on a sales page. One file that gets used beats thirty-six that do not.

instagram.cap:
This is a general warning about the whole information economy, ours included. Counts are seductive and mostly irrelevant.

A seller who talks you down to the smaller pack is a seller you can trust.

facebook.body:
Thirty-six files is not automatically better than six. Only if you use them.

More files is a fact about the product. Not a benefit to you.

The benefit is that one of them is the file you actually needed — and if six would have done it, buy six.

Volume is easy to produce and hard to use, which is why it makes such a good-looking number.

What did you buy for the volume?

posts.topic: Would you buy without seeing inside

tiktok.hook: Nobody would buy without seeing what is inside. Nobody.
beats: It is the same five thousand
tiktok.vo: I asked whether people would pay for something without seeing what was inside. Not one person said yes, and a few were offended by the question. Five thousand naira is not a small amount to the person deciding whether to spend it, which is why the contents page is not generosity. It is the minimum, and most sellers skip it.
tiktok.cap: Nobody buys a mystery box. Five thousand is not small to the person paying it.
tiktok.body: Not one person said yes, and a few were offended by the question. Five thousand naira is not small to the person deciding whether to spend it, which is why a contents page is the minimum, not a favour.

instagram.cap:
The answer was unanimous and slightly annoyed. That reaction is worth remembering the next time you are tempted to hide the contents behind an email form.

Ask your own buyers this question and then do what they say.

facebook.body:
I asked whether people would pay for something without seeing what was inside.

Not one person said yes. A few were offended by the question.

₦5,000 is not a small amount to the person deciding whether to spend it — which is why a contents page is the minimum, not a favour.

What have you bought blind?

posts.why: Refusing filler is a product principle stated out loud.

tiktok.hook: They told us to pad the bundle. We kept the real count.
beats: And then it would be a lie
tiktok.vo: Someone suggested we split the existing files into more files and call the bundle fifty two instead of thirty six, because a bigger number converts better. It would have worked. It would also have meant that every honest count in this account became something you had to check, and the whole reason anyone believes the limits here is that the numbers are real and small. So: thirty six.
tiktok.cap: We could call it 52 files. We would rather the number stayed true.
tiktok.body: Splitting files to inflate the count would have converted better. It would also have made every honest number in this account something a customer had to verify.

instagram.cap:
Every padded count makes the reader recalculate everything else you have said. It is a strange trade: a small lift now for a permanent tax on trust.

An inflated number is a discount on your credibility, paid later.

facebook.body:
Someone suggested we split our existing files into more files and call the bundle 52 instead of 36, because a bigger number converts better.

It would have worked.

It would also have made every honest number in this account something you had to check.

So: thirty-six.

What number would you rather defend?

posts.why: Leaves the buyer with a habit rather than an urge.

tiktok.hook: Check the contents page before you buy. From anyone.
tiktok.vo: Before buying anything from anyone, check the contents page. If there is not one, ask for it. A seller who can produce it in ten minutes is organised. A seller who says it is a surprise is telling you the product is a surprise too, and surprises are how people end up with a folder they never open. Ask for the list. It is a normal question.
tiktok.cap: Ask for the contents page. It is a normal question, not a rude one.
tiktok.body: A seller who can produce a contents page in ten minutes is organised. One who says it is a surprise is telling you something about the product too. Ask for the list.

instagram.cap:
This is the buyer's version of the same advice we give sellers: show the inventory. Both sides get faster, fairer decisions.

The question costs nothing and saves more than any discount code.

facebook.body:
Before buying anything, from anyone, check the contents page.

If there is not one, ask for it.

A seller who can produce it in ten minutes is organised. A seller who says it is a surprise is telling you the product is a surprise too — and surprises are how people end up with a folder they never open.

Ask for the list. It is a normal question.
